extracted.intended_audience: intellectual property attorneys, patent litigators, and clients interested in Federal Circuit patent appeals
extracted.subtask_description: An empirical review that collects and analyzes all patent cases decided by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit during calendar year 2019, with explicit inclusion/exclusion rules and summary metrics (e.g., affirmance rates, IPR appeal share, patent-owner success).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal scope (calendar year 2019)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study 'covers all patent cases decided by the Federal Circuit in 2019.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As in past years, the study is limited to the court's calendar year 2019 decisions and compares 2019 to prior years (2017–2018).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion types included
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes 'precedential opinion, nonprecedential opinion or summary affirmance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All such opinion types are counted in the dataset; the study does not limit analysis to precedential opinions only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision types included
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes 'merits decisions, rulings on writ petitions, and dismissals for unappealable subject matter or lack of constitutional standing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These substantive decision types are treated as part of the Federal Circuit's 2019 patent docket for purposes of the empirical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Excludes 'denials of leave to appeal, stipulated dismissals and remands, and cases remanded to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board in the wake of SAS Institute Inc. v. Iancu or Arthrex Inc. v. Smith & Nephew Inc.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are explicitly removed so that the dataset reflects decided patent cases rather than procedural denials, stipulated dispositions, or PTAB remands tied to specific post-grant developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes review (IPR) appeals proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracks that 'inter partes review appeals consumed an ever-larger portion of the court's docket.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study measures the share of the Federal Circuit's patent docket made up by IPR-related appeals and highlights trends over time (increase relative to prior years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmance rate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a key outcome metric; the article notes that the court's affirmance rate rose in 2019 compared to prior years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner success rate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a central substantive outcome, with the observation that patent owners' success rates 'slipped even further' in 2019.
